raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When an object in `Llama32Detector.detect_and_parse` (`llama3`) fails to decode as JSON, the Python-dict fallback looks for the matching `}` with a character-by-character Python loop starting from the failed start. If the braces never balance, every `{"name":` start rescans to the end of the text:

| Input (one non-streaming parse) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 126 KB of repeated `<|python_tag|>{"name":"` | 38 – 59 s | 0.08 s |
| 120 KB of `{"name": {` | 93 – 108 s | 0.16 s |

Tool-call parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so one such response stalls every in-flight request. Found with an Atheris fuzzing harness that records per-input parse time.

## Modifications

- `_make_brace_matcher`: on the first failed decode, index every brace position and the running brace level once. "The first `}` at or after `idx` that brings the count started at `idx` back to 0" is then "the first `}` at or after `idx` whose global level equals the level just before `idx`", which is a bisect lookup instead of a scan. It returns exactly the position the loop produced (including "no match", which falls back to `idx` as before).
- Regression test `test_unbalanced_braces_parse_in_linear_time` in `test_llama32_detector.py` (fails on `main`, passes here).

Residual: `raw_decode(action_text[idx:])` still slices the remaining text on every failed attempt, a much smaller super-linear term (0.25 s at 120 KB, 0.67 s at 240 KB). Passing `idx` to `raw_decode` instead was slower, because each `JSONDecodeError` counts line numbers from position 0, so this PR leaves it.

## Accuracy Tests

- Brace matcher vs the old loop on 300k random strings, at every start index: identical.
- Differential test of `main` vs patched detector (20k random + 20k mutated well-formed JSON / Python-dict inputs, streaming under random re-chunking and non-streaming): **0 mismatches** (9.5k produced parsed calls).
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/`: 630 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above.

Related: #42573 – #42584 (same issue class in other tool-call parsers).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -1,7 +1,9 @@
+import bisect
 import json
 import logging
 import re
-from typing import List
+from collections import defaultdict
+from typing import Callable, List, Optional
 
 from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Tool
 from sglang.srt.function_call.base_format_detector import BaseFormatDetector
@@ -15,6 +17,29 @@
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
 
+def _make_brace_matcher(text: str) -> Callable[[int], Optional[int]]:
+    # match(idx) -> end of the first "}" at or after idx that brings the running
+    # brace count (started at idx) back to 0, else None; O(log n) per query.
+    brace_pos, levels = [], []
+    closes_by_level = defaultdict(list)
+    level = 0
+    for m in re.finditer(r"[{}]", text):
+        level += 1 if m.group() == "{" else -1
+        brace_pos.append(m.start())
+        levels.append(level)
+        if m.group() == "}":
+            closes_by_level[level].append(m.start())
+
+    def match(idx: int) -> Optional[int]:
+        before = bisect.bisect_left(brace_pos, idx)
+        base = levels[before - 1] if before else 0
+        closes = closes_by_level.get(base, [])
+        i = bisect.bisect_left(closes, idx)
+        return closes[i] + 1 if i < len(closes) else None
+
+    return match
+
+
 class Llama32Detector(BaseFormatDetector):
     """
     Detector for Llama 3.2 models with json tool call format.
@@ -65,6 +90,9 @@ def detect_and_parse(self, text: str, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult
         safe_idx = idx  # the index of the last valid JSON object
         all_actions = []
         action_text_len = len(action_text)
+        # Built on first use; rescanning for the matching brace from every
+        # failed object start is quadratic when braces never balance.
+        match_brace = None
         while idx < action_text_len:
             try:
                 obj, end = decoder.raw_decode(action_text[idx:])
@@ -74,16 +102,9 @@ def detect_and_parse(self, text: str, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult
             except json.JSONDecodeError:
                 # Try Python dict conversion as fallback
                 try:
-                    dict_end = idx
-                    brace_count = 0
-                    for i in range(idx, action_text_len):
-                        if action_text[i] == "{":
-                            brace_count += 1
-                        elif action_text[i] == "}":
-                            brace_count -= 1
-                            if brace_count == 0:
-                                dict_end = i + 1
-                                break
+                    if match_brace is None:
+                        match_brace = _make_brace_matcher(action_text)
+                    dict_end = match_brace(idx) or idx
 
                     if dict_end > idx:
                         potential_dict = action_text[idx:dict_end]

@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 """Unit tests for Llama32Detector — no server, no model loading."""
 
 import json
+import time
 
 from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
 from sglang.srt.function_call.llama32_detector import Llama32Detector
@@ -185,6 +186,22 @@ def test_streaming_text_then_tool_call(self):
         self.assertEqual(params["city"], "Tokyo")
         self.assertEqual(params["unit"], "celsius")
 
+    def test_unbalanced_braces_parse_in_linear_time(self):
+        """Many object starts whose braces never balance must not stall the
+        parser (it runs on the event loop); a valid call before them parses."""
+        text = (
+            '<|python_tag|>{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}};'
+            + '{"name": {' * 7000
+        )
+
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        result = self.detector.detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+
+        self.assertLess(elapsed, 1.0)
+        self.assertEqual(len(result.calls), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.calls[0].parameters), {"city": "Paris"})
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     import unittest
